prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (RDC; call sign Juniper) provides 24/7 EMS intake, pediatric/adult triage support, ambulance dispatch/coordination, surge declaration, mutual-aid coordination and regional coverage picture under approved protocols; jurisdictions retain ownership/local policy. Call Taker Mara records caller reports and, for pediatrics, obtains age, available weight and caregiver observations; verifies arrival time against timeline/comms after Bedside Arrival Receipt. Computer Aided Dispatch Console checks locations and displays incident/priority/travel/availability/access/staging/surge/facility constraints. Ambulance Coordination Platform consolidates unit position/status with timestamps, presents matching units/destinations/instructions, and tracks accepted mutual-aid separately from local staffed resources. Radio Coordinator Mistral uses Regional Radio Network/talkgroups to send assignments/hazards/routes/destinations, coverage bulletins, mutual-aid requests/acceptances/updates; requires crew repeat-back/ack, retries/alerts, directs approved fallback channels during primary-channel outage. Crews acknowledge fallback assignments and repeat critical location/destination before moving. Paramedic Crew/Ambulance Unit 417 reports status/location/conflicts/hazards/delays/staging/arrival/handover, acknowledges destination, requests renewed consultation, reassesses pediatric patients en route and reports material changes to receiving facility; Unit 417 may be reassigned only after dispatch confirms patient-care/transport obligations permit. Fleet Maintenance Cell Bluejay promptly reports unavailable/restricted vehicles and Battery Swap Voucher; dispatch must not count unavailable units. Hospital Liaison Desk Kestrel obtains/records facility capacity/contact/constraints/responses, ED consults, restrictions, Bedside Arrival Receipt and Pediatric Acuity Note; shall confirm pediatric service limits/capacity are communicated before final destination and keep dispatch informed of unresolved constraints. Emergency Department staff acknowledge destination changes and immediate access restrictions, clarify identity/transfer docs. Riverside Trauma Center advises Kestrel when trauma intake affects destination suitability. North Gate Status Board/South Gate Status Board provide current access views; South produces South Access Lane Notice. Surge begins when approved thresholds cross; Triage Supervisor validates prioritization and reviews audit memo before duplicate closure. Regional Medical Director Copperfield approves temporary triage overrides/rationales and protocol adjustments. Shift Commander Sundial approves exceptions, mutual-aid release, escalations, and post-surge handover of assignments/constraints/staffing gaps. Data Quality Officer resolves discrepancies without delaying care. RDC degraded-radio procedure prioritizes emergency traffic/common picture; network operators announce

New part:
S202: If voice contact fails, dispatchers use the approved data channel when available and record the time of each attempted contact.
S203: Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays the latest confirmed unit status alongside the time and source of that confirmation.
S204: Ambulance Coordination Platform preserves queued status updates during brief connection interruptions and flags records that require reconciliation.
S205: Coverage monitoring compares successful radio checks with the planned check interval for each operating area.
S206: North Gate Status Board and South Gate Status Board provide separate views of access conditions that may affect radio reach or ambulance movement.
S207: Radio Coordinator uses the change card to adjust channel assignments and record the effective time of each change.
S208: Shift Commander receives the Coverage Gap Bulletin and decides whether staffing or deployment adjustments are needed.
S209: Data Quality Officer reviews Pebble for conflicting timestamps before interrupted communications are reconciled.
S210: Triage Supervisor identifies calls whose clinical priority requires immediate radio access and communicates that priority to dispatch staff.
S211: Call Taker Mara keeps the caller connected when feasible while dispatch staff attempt to reach the assigned crew through an approved alternate channel.
S212: Ambulance Unit 417 reports its last confirmed position and safe operating status as soon as contact is restored.
S213: Fleet Maintenance Cell reports radio equipment faults through the established maintenance escalation path.
S214: Hospital Liaison Desk uses available telephone channels to confirm whether receiving facilities can accept arrivals during a network disruption.
S215: Emergency Department staff receive concise arrival updates through the approved backup contact method when radio delivery is unavailable.
S216: Regional Medical Director may advise on clinical prioritization when communication limits materially affect response choices.
S217: Paramedic Crew members follow local safety procedures and do not enter an area where dispatch instructions cannot be confirmed if conditions are uncertain.
S218: Shift Commander retains operational authority until a named successor acknowledges the handover or a higher-level incident command arrangement takes effect.
S219: The outgoing shift records active incidents, communication failures, temporary channel assignments, and decisions awaiting review.
S220: The incoming shift verifies open assignments and confirms which communication paths remain available before accepting control.
S221: After service is restored, dispatch staff reconcile delayed status reports against their recorded timestamps and preserve any unresolved discrepancy for review.
S222: The Regional Dispatch Center maintains controlled procedures for reviewing operational records, approving system changes, and documenting corrective actions.
S223: The Data Quality Officer samples incident records for completeness, timestamp consistency, and alignment between dispatch decisions and recorded outcomes.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
